description: The P2P override covers host-facing transfers as well as inter-GPU copies, so it can add output even in a single-GPU configuration.
trigger: Import with a nonempty EXLLAMA_NO_P2P_COPY and pass a CPU tensor to a module on a GPU, or a GPU tensor to a module on CPU. For example, Model._load_single honors the embedding's prefer_cpu capability while placing ordinary modules on the selected GPU; Model.forward passes state across that boundary.
expected_behavior: If the option only bypassed peer-to-peer GPU copies, a transfer with a CPU endpoint would retain the original quiet to(self.device) path.
actual_behavior: Any device mismatch takes the enabled branch. It prints a dot before calling cpu().to(self.device), even if the source or destination is already CPU.

verification.description: Compared the new predicate with the parent helper and inspected model placement and the parent call sites. The difference applies only when an inspected caller supplies a mismatched device while the override is enabled.
verification.limits: This establishes branch scope, not that PyTorch makes an extra physical copy when an endpoint is already on CPU.

verification.description: Fake CPU-to-GPU and GPU-to-CPU cases both recorded cpu(), to(...), and one dot line with the override enabled.
verification.limits: No real tensors, model execution, or GPU transfers.

introductions.rationale: The new opt-in branch checks device inequality and prints a dot before staging, so any mismatch with a CPU endpoint enters it.
